message.reasoning:
We need to generate new test cases for untested input combinations, avoiding duplication with existing cases. Existing groups cover:

- Matching known VersionFlag ids (two examples)
- Unnormalized $schema URIs containing "json-schema.org/draft" with various substrings: draft-07, /draft/2019-09/, /draft/2020-12/, /draft-04/, /draft-06/, and a case where contains "json-schema.org/draft" but none of specific substrings (draft-05) -> unchanged.
- No normalization needed (does not contain draft marker): urn:custom:schema, empty string.
- Edge case null input -> NPE.

Missing test cases:

- IDs that contain "://json-schema.org/draft" but also contain multiple matching substrings? Eg contains both draft-07 and draft-06? Not realistic but we can test order: method checks in order: if contains "/draft-07/", else if "/draft/2019-09/", else if "/draft/2020-12/", else if "/draft-04/", else if "/draft-06/". So if string contains both "/draft-07/" and "/draft-06/", first condition matches draft-07. Test that precedence works.

- IDs that contain "://json-schema.org/draft" but with uppercase variations? The method uses case-sensitive contains, so uppercase won't match. Test that unchanged.

- IDs that contain "://json-schema.org/draft" but with extra path after recognized substring, e.g., ".../draft-07/extra". Should still replace entire id with V7 because condition only checks contains substring; it will replace.

- IDs that contain "://json-schema.org/draft" but missing trailing slash after version? e.g., ".../draft-07". The condition checks "/draft-07/". So not matched, unchanged.

- IDs that contain "json-schema.org/draft" but not preceded by "://". E.g., "http://example.com/json-schema.org/draft-07/schema". The outer if checks id.contains("://json-schema.org/draft") . This string does not contain "://json-schema.org/draft", so no normalization. Test that unchanged.

- IDs that are already normalized but also contain "://json-schema.org/draft" but not exactly matching VersionFlag ids (maybe extra fragment). For example "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#extra". It contains "://json-schema.org/draft" and "/draft-07/". Since not found in VersionFlag (since VersionFlag ids are exact). So it will go into unnormalized block and replace with V7. So test that.

- IDs that match a VersionFlag but also contain other substrings; the method will find in first loop and set found true, then skip unnormalized block. So test that precedence.

- Test that method returns same string object? Not needed.

- Test with whitespace trimmed? Not part.

- Test with id containing "://json-schema.org/draft" but with different protocol like "ftp://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema". Contains "://json-schema.org/draft"? Yes includes "://json-schema.org/draft". So should normalize to V7.

- Test with id that contains "://json-schema.org/draft" but is a full URL with query parameters: ".../draft-07/schema?foo=bar". Should still normalize.

- Test with id containing both "/draft/2019-09/" and "/draft-07/". The order picks draft-07 first.

- Also test that method does not modify when id is a known VersionFlag but also contains other substrings (should return unchanged). Already covered maybe not.

Thus we need to produce new test groups.

Let's propose groups:

1. "Normalization precedence when multiple draft substrings present"
   Cases:
   - id = "https://example.com/draft-07/path/draft-06/schema.json" -> expected V7 (SchemaId.V7)
   - id = "https://example.com/draft/2019-09/path/draft-07/schema" -> expected V7 because contains "/draft-07/" check first? Actually order: check draft-07 first, then draft/2019-09. The string contains "/draft-07/" so V7.

2. "Case sensitivity of draft marker"
   Cases:
   - id = "HTTPS://json-schema.org/DRAFT-07/schema#" (uppercase) -> expected unchanged because contains "://json-schema.org/draft" is case-sensitive, not found. Also not a VersionFlag (since VersionFlag ids are lower case). So unchanged.

3. "Missing trailing slash after version substring"
   Cases:
   - id = "https://example.com/draft-07schema" (no slash) -> unchanged.
   - id = "https://example.com/draft-07" -> unchanged.

4. "Draft marker without required prefix"
   Cases:
   - id = "http://example.com/json-schema.org/draft-07/schema" -> unchanged.

5. "Normalization with non-http scheme (ftp)"
   Cases:
   - id = "ftp://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema" -> expected V7.

6. "Normalization with query parameters and fragment"
   Cases:
   - id = "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema?foo=bar#section" -> expected V7 (SchemaId.V7). Ensure that method replaces entire id.

7. "Already normalized but with extra fragment"
   Cases:
   - id = "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#extra" -> expected V7 (since not exact match). This tests that method still normalizes.

8. "Known VersionFlag takes precedence over unnormalized detection"
   Cases:
   - id = "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" (exact match) already covered. Maybe need a case where id matches VersionFlag but also contains other substrings like "/draft-04/". Not possible because VersionFlag id is exact string. But we can test "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#/something" which is not exact match, so will go to unnormalized block. Already covered in #7.

9. "Empty string with draft marker but no version"
   Cases:
   - id = "http://json-schema.org/draft/" -> contains "://json-schema.org/draft" but none of specific substrings, should remain unchanged.

10. "Null input already covered."

Make sure not duplicate existing.

Now produce JSON output.

Need to reference SchemaId constants values. In code, SchemaId.V7 etc. We need actual string values. Not given but typical: SchemaId.V7 = "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#" ; V201909 = "http://json-schema.org/draft/2019-09/schema#" ; V202012 = "http://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema#" ; V4 = "http://json-schema.org/draft-04/schema#" ; V6 = "http://json-schema.org/draft-06/schema#" . Use those.
